pitcher_strikeouts.rederivation_notes: My own chain, written from the KXMLBKS text before opening the author's stages. (1) Start gate: the text only defines two states, scratched or not a starter (pays the undefined 'fair market price') versus starter with at least one batter faced (settles on strikeouts); relief excluded. (2) Batters-faced exposure: pitch budget, manager hook, performance and game-state exits, opener or bulk plans, October short leashes (the sample is an Oct 28 2026 World Series game). (3) Per-PA K probability: pitcher arsenal and count-level whiff/called-strike skill against the confirmed nine by handedness, times-through-order, plus zone, framing and ABS challenge effects, park/weather. (4) Overdispersion from a start-level latent and K/BF pitch-cost coupling. (5) Nested N+ rungs, monotone. Required inputs I expected: confirmed starter and opener flag, expected-BF survival curve, pitcher-side K skill with priors, confirmed lineup whiff, zone-regime data, own/opponent run environment for game states. Differences after reading: the author's stages 1-5 match this chain and are strong (hazard curve, two-strike putaway, dispersion are good additions). Missed or wrong: the 2026 ABS challenge regime is absent; 'fair market price' is called a refund; no pregame run-environment input for game-state exits; a few unsupported step and threshold shapes.

findings.text: ABS regime missing. MLB ran the ABS ball-strike challenge system in all 2026 regular-season and postseason games (web check: 2 challenges per team, ball touching any part of the zone is a strike), and the sampled game (Oct 28 2026) is inside it. Stage s4 ('Zone, catcher and environment shifts'), interaction 'umpire_k_bb_effect x catcher_framing x battery_assignment' and the nonlinearity story all treat human-umpire zone and framing as the zone mechanism, with 3-season windows and UmpScorecards history that pre-date ABS. Required change: add a 2026+ zone-regime input (challenge availability and usage, batter/pitcher/catcher challenge success, effective zone definition) and treat umpire/framing history as a pre-2026 regime with its own shrinkage; the record never mentions ABS.

Settlement mischaracterised. The rules say 'If Drew Rasmussen is scratched or is not a starting pitcher, the market will resolve to the fair market price.' The record repeatedly calls this a 'refund' / 'void-style refund' and says a scratch is 'outside the settled distribution' (s1, settlement_definition, interaction 2). The text defines neither the price nor when it is struck, so a scratch is a priced settlement value that changes P&L for every holder; it is not a refund at entry. 'fair market price' is not listed as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS in unresolved (only postponement and source are). Required change: add an unresolved entry for the fair-price definition and stop treating scratch risk as outside the modelled payoff.

Zero-batter starter undefined. The text defines starter-with-at-least-one-batter-faced and scratch/non-starter, but not a starter who throws pitches and leaves (injury, ejection, rain) before facing a batter. variants_and_edge_cases and s1 do not list it, while the sibling ERHW record asserts 'immediate injury still settles on tiny counts' and the unreg record says walks refund; the K record should flag it CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.

No pregame game-script input. The hazard curve conditions on runs allowed, lead/deficit and runners, but the record states these 'enter only inside a simulation, not as pregame data'. A simulation needs a run-scoring model (own offence vs opponent starter/bullpen, opponent offence vs this pitcher) that no listed input supplies; game_context_script coverage is only the hazard curve and postseason usage. Add a non-market team run-environment input (own lineup wRC+ by hand, opposing bullpen quality) or state the gap.

Audit/role issues. m.ladder_structure is marked BENCHMARK_ONLY and left unused, but rung construction (floor_strike, 'greater' N-0.5, nesting, monotonicity) is contract metadata, not a market-derived value; only rung prices are. mlb.pa_sim (a simulator, not an input), mlb.news and mlb.postseason_leverage_usage are used in stages/data feeds but appear in neither input_audit nor new_inputs here. m.quote_history and mlb.platoon are audited but used nowhere.

Unsupported shape claims. Nonlinearity 'Step function at the batter-18/19 and 27/28 boundaries, not a slope' and 'threshold about -1 mph' velocity are asserted as facts; the audit of mlb.tto itself says pitcher-specific decay is more informative, and TTO penalties are commonly estimated as per-batter/familiarity gradients. These should be MECHANISM_UNCERTAIN in unresolved; the numeric constants (0.15-0.40, 1 mph) have no cited basis.

Talent-prior gap. Pitcher-side talent rests on k_rates, pitch_type_whiff and a 120-BF half-life, with no stuff/pitch-model quality measure or projection-system K% prior for arsenal changes (new sweeper/splitter), returns from injury or rookies, which is exactly where pitch-level whiff samples are thinnest. Add a pitch-quality/projection prior or disclose the gap.

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: exit state (runners, score at exit) is attributed to 'Retrosheet / Baseball-Reference game logs ... derived from event files'. Retrosheet event files are released after the season, so they cannot give as-of in-season hazard-curve fits; only MLB Stats API play-by-play can, and the record does not say so.

pitcher_outs.rederivation_notes: My own chain from the KXMLBOUTS text (it sits in the unreg bucket; this key has no live series). Settlement: starter who records at least one pitch settles on outs recorded; scratched/non-starter pays fair market price; relief excluded. Mechanism: outs = sum over batters faced of P(out) plus double-play and baserunning outs, truncated by the first exit stopping time: pitch budget (cap or workload), pitch cost per out, performance hook (runs/traffic), inning-end and third-time-through conventions, opener plans, rain-delay removal, October leash. Distribution: lattice in thirds, spikes at 15/18, left tail of blow-ups. Inputs I expected: opener/probable flag, expected pitch count and cap, pitches per out, confirmed lineup and opponent OBP/contact/DP proneness, defence, manager hook habits with run state, bullpen state, rest, weather/delay, plus own and opponent run environment. After reading: the author's exit_boundary_mass, outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning and delay_starter_removal are strong. Missed: no confirmed-lineup/opponent offence input at all, no handling of 2026 ABS effects on pitch cost, and a series-to-archetype mapping hole that leaves the settlement category unverified.

findings.text: Series mapping hole. The only outs ladder (KXMLBOUTS, 'greater 14.5') is filed under unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials; this key has live_series [] and rules_evidence []. settlement_contract is marked NOT_APPLICABLE with the reason that no ledger series is classified here, which is wrong for an archetype whose single most decisive fact is the contract gate ('records at least one pitch', unlike strikeouts' one batter faced). The same text and quote are re-derived in the unreg record. Required change: map KXMLBOUTS here (or drop this key) and mark settlement_contract COVERED with the verbatim one-pitch quote, so the gate is not verified only in a sibling bucket.

Missing lineup/opponent-offence input. No input represents the confirmed batting order or opposing offence: mlb.lineup_pit, mlb.platoon and team_wrc_vs_hand are absent from existing and new inputs. Yet s3 relies on 'the lineup's on-base and double-play proneness', outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning is 'as-of lineup post', and input_audit says 'lineup is unknown until the card posts'. Outs per batter depend directly on the nine hitters (OBP, K, GIDP rate, speed), so the primary mechanism has no named lineup input and no lineup-vintage handling. Add lineup/opposing-offence inputs by hand.

No pregame game-script input and officiating dismissed by circular reasoning: officiating_rules NOT_APPLICABLE argues 'the zone effect is already inside pitches per PA', but pitches per PA is a history-based pitcher/opponent average that cannot contain the day's zone regime. In 2026 MLB used ABS challenges in every game, which shifts walks, called strikes and thus pitch cost per out; this is undiscussed. Also no input drives the run state the hook reacts to (own offence vs opposing staff).

Role mislabels. pitch_count_limit is KEEP_PRIMARY 'main driver on limited-return starts', but the record also says the cap 'never binds' for uncapped starters; for most starts it is irrelevant, so it is a regime gate (secondary) with an announced-cap data field, not a primary continuous input. The same exit-hazard object is named leash/sp_workload here, sp_hook_hazard_curve in the strikeout record and exit_boundary_mass in outs: one shared hazard model is being specified under three ids across sibling archetypes.

Unverified rung claim. variants_and_edge_cases speak of '16 outs, 17 outs rungs' and rungs 'on multiples of three'; the sampled evidence shows only 15+ (floor 14.5). The set of listed rungs is not established. Counting claims (outs on DPs and caught stealing credited to the pitcher on the mound) are box-score convention, not contract text, and should be marked as presumed.

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED fields: 'Retrosheet game logs' are listed for start logs with exit state (game logs do not carry exit inning/out/runners; event files do, and lag the season); the PA event log lists outs_on_play and pitches-in-PA, which are not Statcast CSV columns (outs must be derived from outs_when_up differences). Stats API is the only as-of in-season source.

Invented constants presented as mechanism: 'pitches per PA above about 4.2', 'cap 85-110 pitches', 'out probability about 0.68-0.78', 'delay probability a few percent' have no cited basis; interaction 2 states managers 'nearly never' pull at outs 19-20, an empirical claim not backed here (unresolved outs_exit_lattice_stability covers persistence but not the level).

pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks.rederivation_notes: My own chain from KXMLBERA/KXMLBWA text (hits allowed, KXMLBHA, is title-only and filed under the hitter hits/total-bases bucket). Settlement: starter with at least one batter faced settles on the stat; scratch/non-starter pays fair market price; relief excluded. Mechanism: batters faced from the hook; per-PA outcome multinomial (K, BB/HBP, HR, ball in play); BIP to hits via contact quality, defence, park; walks via command vs patience and the zone (ABS in 2026); earned runs via base-out sequencing, HR with traffic, LOB, unearned reconstruction and inherited runners the bullpen lets score; positive dependence between H, BB, ER through shared latent command; runs truncate the outing (endogenous exposure). Inputs expected: confirmed lineup and handedness, pitcher contact/BB/HR profile with priors, defence, park by hand, bullpen after exit, zone regime, scorer behaviour. After reading: the author's baserunner_to_run_conversion, er_ur_scoring_split and inherited_runner_charge_risk are good. Missed or wrong: ABS, hits-allowed series mapping and rule overclaim, ladder-specific roles, several audit verdicts that contradict their own reasons.

findings.text: Series mapping and overclaim. Zero live series here: KXMLBERA and KXMLBWA are in unreg, and KXMLBHA ('Pro Baseball Hits Allowed', TITLE_ONLY, type player_prop:hits_tb) is filed under the hitter hits/total-bases archetype where hitter-side inputs would be applied to a pitcher count. settlement_definition says 'The sampled rules ... settle on the recorded stat once he has faced at least one batter' for all three ladders, but no hits-allowed rules text was sampled (the unresolved item admits this). The hits ladder's gate, source and tie/void wording are therefore unverified, not VERIFIED. Required change: split hits-allowed out as TITLE_ONLY/CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS and fix the ledger mapping.

2026 ABS regime absent for walks/ER. Walk probability is driven by called balls and strikes; the record's walk mechanism (umpire zone x framing x chase, interaction 2 'convex', nonlinearity 'zone rate below 42%') ignores that every 2026 game used ABS challenges (verified by web search). The umpire and catcher_framing inputs and UmpScorecards data pre-date it. Add a zone-regime input and treat historical umpire/framing effects as a different regime.

Unsupported 'settlement' facts. The settlement_definition asserts walks include intentional but not hit batters, inherited runners are charged to the starter, hits follow scorer rulings, and that an 'opener or immediate injury still settles on tiny counts'. None of this is in sampled text for these ladders; the zero-batter starter case is undefined by the rules (and the unreg record says walks 'refund' in that case, contradicting this record). Mark as presumed scoring convention and add CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS for the zero-BF starter.

Single role per input across three different ladders. plate_discipline and contact_defense are both KEEP_PRIMARY though each is primary for only one ladder (walks vs hits); pitcher_hr_vulnerability primary only for ER. Roles should be per ladder, otherwise the required-input list cannot be filtered for a given series (the audit text even says contact_defense is 'secondary for walks (none)').

Audit verdicts contradict their reasons. team_wrc_vs_hand is KEEP_SECONDARY while the reason says 'a lineup-specific PA-level matchup replaces it'; mlb.defense is DUPLICATE_OF catcher_framing though the reason says the OAA part is a distinct driver belonging in contact_defense; mlb.contact_dist is WEAK ('wrong object for pitcher counts') but is still in s5 and in the PA-event feeds_inputs; mlb.pa_sim is 'a simulation engine, not an input' yet KEEP_SECONDARY and used as stage input. Weak/duplicate inputs left in the working set.

SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: 'runs_scored_on_play' is listed as a Statcast field (Statcast has bat_score/post_bat_score and delta_run_exp; runs on play must be derived); official-scorer identity per game and post-game scoring changes are flagged but the new input official_scorer_hit_error_tendency still defaults to 'primary-style' park tendencies without evidence scorers persist; er_ur_scoring_split is categorised 'officiating' though it is a fielding/defence quantity.

offfield_markets.rederivation_notes: My own chain from the sampled rules. KXMLBNLMOTY/ALMOTY and KXMLBEOTY: pay on the official award winner; electorates differ (BBWAA writers for managers; the MLB Executive of the Year is a club vote), ballots precede the postseason. KXMLBTEAMSALE: pays only if the deal is finalized and approved by the league before Jan 1 2027, so process stage and league approval timing drive it. KXMLBDELAY: any official weather delay (start delay or stoppage) in a named game: forecast precipitation/lightning timing, roof, park history. KXMLBBGAME: Mobile Legends match winner (rating model; 48-hour postponement and cancellation pay fair price). KXMLBCOACH: next manager, a vacancy plus identity-selection process (title only). Required inputs: per-family voter/electorate and standings-vs-expectation features, sale stage hazard, weather vintage, esports ratings, hiring candidate pool. After reading: the family decomposition and sale-stage hazard are good. Missed or wrong: executive voters are misdescribed, KXMLBCOACH has no mechanism or input, delay inputs are borrowed unaudited, and benchmark/weak inputs still sit in stages and interactions.

findings.text: Executive-of-the-Year electorate wrong. s2 says manager AND executive of the year 'are decided by a ballot of writers' (and the voter-model unresolved item assumes writers). The MLB Executive of the Year award is voted by the 30 clubs before the postseason (web check; the Sporting News version is voted by executives), not by BBWAA writers; the sampled KXMLBEOTY text names no electorate ('Governing League'). A club/executive electorate (self-vote exclusion, peer perception of roster construction) changes the voter model, the data (no public writer-style ballots) and the primary feature manager_wins_over_expectation, which is manager-centric. Fix the claim or mark SOURCE_UNVERIFIED.

KXMLBCOACH has no mechanism or input. The summary mentions 'a hiring hazard conditional on a vacancy and the candidate pool', but stages s2-s5 have no hiring stage and new_inputs defines nothing for it (manager_firing_hazard exists only in the transactions record). Next-manager resolves per candidate, so a candidate-pool/identity-selection input (interviews reported, GM or coach connections, internal vs external, seniority) is required and absent. off_family_routing only says the series is title-only.

Mapping and borrowed inputs. The three KXMLBDELAY ids mlb.delay_risk, mlb.forecast_precip_timing and mlb.roof_state are used in s4 and required_data but are neither defined in this record nor audited; category_coverage lists environment as COVERED only by mlb.news and says delay inputs are 'routed to the extras_and_delay record', contradicting s4. Award series are split inconsistently across the ledger (MOTY/EOTY here, ROTY/MVP in leaders_and_awards, Reliever of the Year in season_futures), and an esports match (not baseball) is carried under an mlb. prefix. The required input set for three of seven series therefore lives in other archetypes.

Weak and benchmark items left in the working set. mlb.offfield_base_rate is WEAK ('meaningless') yet appears in s2, three interactions, a nonlinearity and distribution_variance coverage; m.external_lines, m.quote_history, m.volume_oi are BENCHMARK_ONLY but are listed as stage input_ids (s5) and as members of interactions 3 and 4, so market-derived values enter the input structure. m.rules_text is used as an 'interacting input' (interactions 3-4), which are really calibration checks of news credibility against rules wording, not input interactions.

Unsupported esports premises. Interaction 3 and the rating input assume best-of-3 vs best-of-5 formats and 'concave' compression, but the sampled KXMLBBGAME text says only 'the full match' with no format; the nonlinearity describes the same relation as 'S-shaped' while the interaction says 'concave'. Glicko roster-reset (30%) and patch-inflation constants are invented. This is a non-baseball market whose inputs cannot be checked against any sampled rule beyond the 48-hour refund.

KXMLBDELAY edge cases: the rule counts a game 'officially delayed due to weather' (start delay or stoppage); the record notes postponement without play is undescribed but gives no treatment for a game postponed before first pitch, which is the dominant forecast-driven outcome, and the roof-closed case. Add as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS with a pre-game-window requirement in the forecast data.

player_participation.rederivation_notes: My own chain from KXMLBSTART / KXMLBPITCH / KXMLBNEXTTEAM text. KXMLBSTART: Yes only if the player is in the official starting batting order when the game begins (replacement before first pitch resolves No; pinch hitting does not count; the DH counts). Chain: roster/health gate, manager decision (role, platoon vs opposing starter hand, rest, DH usage, travel, postseason all-in policy), lineup-card posting, late-scratch and late-insertion hazard. KXMLBPITCH: at least one pitch in a regular-season game inside a date window: rehab/availability survival plus team plan (two-way player). KXMLBNEXTTEAM: free-agency or trade destination with Retires/No Team. KXMLBSTARTER (MLB Starting Pitcher) is a probable-pitcher/rotation question. Inputs expected: card vintage and posting time, role and platoon, opposing probable starter hand, injury and rehab stage, schedule, playoff roster state, rotation slot for pitchers, contract status for moves. After reading: the single-game start model and the rehab/window survival are strong. Missed: pitcher-start mechanism, playoff-regime inputs, truncated rule clause, and the CBA lockout effect on moves.

findings.text: Half the live series have no mechanism here. KXMLBSTARTER ('MLB Starting Pitcher'), KXMLBDEBUT and KXMLBNEXTTEAM (and by title KXMLBSTARTINGLINEUP) are covered only by 'should be modelled in the transactions archetype' (s5) or by a rotation arithmetic term (N/5) inside window_exposure_schedule. A starting-pitcher participation market is driven by rotation slot, days of rest, announced probables, skip/six-man/opener usage and staff injuries, none of which is an input; the hitter lineup-card chain (platoon, catcher rest, DH rotation) does not describe it. Debut needs 40-man/call-up inputs. Add pitcher-rotation and call-up inputs or remap the series.

Truncated rules and missing settlement cases. The sampled KXMLBSTART rules_secondary is cut at 'An actual plate appearance is ' so a clause that may change settlement (whether a plate appearance is needed) is unseen; the record treats rules as PARTIALLY_VERIFIED without flagging the cut, and lists no CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS for postponement/suspension although the text says 'originally scheduled'. Late insertion (a bench player enters the card after posting because a teammate is scratched) resolves Yes by the text but is modelled only as a No-hazard.

Postseason regime missing. Both single-game samples (KXMLBSTART Oct 14 2026) are playoff games, but the model's rest/clinched policy, rest_day_patterns and rest_travel are regular-season constructs; October has no clinch-rest, stars rarely sit, round-specific rosters change eligibility, and off days alter pitching plans. Add a postseason round/playoff-roster input or restrict the claim to regular season.

CBA/lockout regime for NEXTTEAM/DEBUT. Free-agent signing before Mar 25 2027 and any 2027 call-up depend on the CBA that expires Dec 1 2026, with a lockout widely expected (web check; the 2021-22 lockout froze 40-man transactions until Mar 10 2022). Not in this record or in transactions.

Source and constant issues: 'MiLB rehab-assignment logs (MLB Stats API)' is listed as exposing rehab stage; whether the Stats API distinguishes rehab assignments is not verified (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED), and bullpen/throwing stages come only from beat reports. The 1-3% late-scratch rate and 0.9/0.3-0.7/0.1 start probabilities are invented. 'opponent_matchup NOT_APPLICABLE' relies on the opposing starter's hand via platoon, but no input carries the opposing probable starter's identity or its announcement vintage.

season_futures.rederivation_notes: My own chain from the sampled win-total, seed, qualifier and MVP/leader rules. KXMLBWINS: regular-season wins only, ties not wins; N+ ladder. Chain: team talent posterior (projection prior plus run differential), injuries/deadline shifts, remaining schedule and opponent mix, binomial game noise, standings/tiebreaker logic, 12-team bracket with byes and fixed seeds (KXMLBSEEDWIN is a union over both leagues' 6 seeds), series win via rotation/rest/bullpen, short-series compression. Award/MVP/leader series (WSMVP co-winner $1/N; LEADERPLAYOFF playoff-only stats, tie proportional payout) need different models: series MVP is conditional on the winning team plus credit-share; playoff leaders need games played in the postseason. Required inputs: talent posterior, schedule state, tiebreaker state, playoff roster/rotation, award electorates. After reading: the talent-posterior, tiebreaker/seed path and postseason rating inputs are good. Missed: ~14 of 53 series have no inputs, a market-derived input is used in the award stage, internal numeric inconsistencies, and borrowed unaudited ids.

findings.text: Award, MVP, leader and bracket series have no inputs. Of the 53 live series about 14 are RELOTY (x2), WSMVP, ALCSMVP, NLCSMVP, ALCY, NLCY, HAARON (x2), LEADERPLAYOFF, MATCHUP, PLAYOFFHOST and similar; stage s5 defers them to season_leaders_and_awards and its only input_ids are mlb.news and m.external_lines. m.external_lines is audited BENCHMARK_ONLY and is a market-derived price, yet it is the stage's input. Series MVPs need P(team wins the series) times a credit-share model, KXMLBLEADERPLAYOFF needs a distribution of playoff games played and PA, MATCHUP/PLAYOFFHOST need bracket-path enumeration; none is specified. sf_mixed_families notes the mixing but does not give the required inputs.

Numeric inconsistency in team_talent_posterior_uncertainty. Posterior mean uses w = n/(n+80) (k = 80), but the stated variance 1/(1/s0^2 + n/s_game^2) with s0 = 0.04 and s_game^2 = 0.25 implies k = s_game^2/s0^2 about 156; and the stage claim 'sd falling ... to about 0.015 in September' is not reproduced by the formula (about 0.029 at n = 140). The measurement as written is internally inconsistent and cannot be implemented as specified.

Misdescribed nonlinearity. pythag_luck is labelled 'Concave: win% as a function of run ratio with exponent about 1.83'; the Pythagorean form is a logistic in log run ratio, nearly linear in run differential across normal ranges, and the claimed concavity at 'large ratios' is irrelevant to season totals. The relevant nonlinearity is the shrinkage weight by games played, which is a different input.

Borrowed unaudited ids and missing state variable. mlb.series_game_state and m.rules_text are used (stages, coverage, data feeds) without being defined or audited here; mlb.season_sim is called 'a method ... not an input' and then used as stage input, while wins to date, games remaining and run differential to date (the primary state of a win-total ladder) are not defined as an input beyond pythag_luck.

Tiebreaker and bracket claims unverified. The seed tiebreaker order ('head-to-head, intradivision, intraleague, last-half record') is a paraphrase with no source cited and no SOURCE_UNVERIFIED entry; fixed bracket (no reseeding) matters for KXMLBMATCHUP and is not stated. Title-only series (AL, NL, WS, divisions) are acknowledged but their tie/cancellation wording is only listed as unseen.

season_leaders_and_awards.rederivation_notes: My own chain from KXMLBAWARDFIN and KXMLBNLROTY text plus the series list. AWARDFIN: finalist per the Source Agencies, and all markets resolve No if finalists are not announced before the winner; the finalist event is top-three of the vote. Winner awards: ballots by an electorate that differs by award (BBWAA for MVP/Cy Young/ROY/MOY; a panel of retired relievers for Reliever of the Year; clubs for Executive; fans plus panel for Hank Aaron; managers/coaches for Gold Glove and Silver Slugger), cast before the postseason. Stat races: current total plus rate times opportunity times availability, order statistic, qualification rules, ties. Others: All-Star selection, All-Star Game outcome/MVP, HR Derby round, draft lottery, Triple Crown. Required inputs: eligibility, ROS projection, availability, electorate-specific ballot model, calendar, qualification rules. After reading: AWARDFIN timing, roy_eligibility and the Plackett-Luce model are good. Missed or wrong: electorate misstatement, qualification-rule claim, six series with no mechanism.

findings.text: Electorate misstated. variants_and_edge_cases says 'BBWAA ballots for MVP, Cy Young, ROY, Manager and Reliever awards'. The Rivera/Hoffman Reliever of the Year awards are voted by a panel of retired relievers (nine all-time relievers, 5-3-1 ballots; web check), not by BBWAA; Hank Aaron, Comeback Player and the executive award also differ. The voter model, 'BBWAA ballots free published after the fact' data source and the claim that one Plackett-Luce model with shared coefficients (k = 3 seasons across awards) serves all awards do not hold for these. Specify electorate per award.

Six or more live series have no stage or input: KXMLBALLSTAR (fan vote, player vote, commissioner/roster rules), KXMLBASGAME ('Professional Baseball All-Star Game', a game-result market), KXMLBASGMVP (conditional on winning team and playing time), KXMLBHRDERBYR1LEAD (swing-time contest), KXMLBDRAFTPICK (lottery odds by record; the variants mention a lottery but no input exists) and KXMLBAWARDCOMBO (joint of awards, needs correlation). s1-s5 and new_inputs address only ROY/finalists/monthly windows/Triple Crown. lea_title_only is generic and does not list these gaps per series.

Qualification claim likely contradicts the official rule. The nonlinearity and interaction state rate leaders have 'zero' probability below 3.1 PA per team game ('Hard threshold'). Official Baseball Rule 9.22 lets a player below the PA minimum still win the title if his rate remains highest after hitless at-bats are added to reach the minimum (and similarly for ERA with earned runs added); I could not verify the current wording by search, so this is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED, but the record's hard-zero treatment would mis-specify borderline candidates and the required PA-shortfall data. Verify the rule and the contract's own qualification wording.

ROY thresholds flagged SOURCE_UNVERIFIED are partly outdated: 'excluding IL and September-expansion days' refers to an expansion exemption that no longer applies with fixed 26-man rosters; eligibility is by MLB service (IL days excluded), not by 'before the season' alone. The 'SOURCE_UNVERIFIED' flag is honest but the mechanism text is stated as 'current rule'.

Weak/duplicate inputs left in. hitter_quality is KEEP_SECONDARY while its reason says it is 'duplicative of the projection input'; hrfb_regression is WEAK ('subsumed by rate projection') yet is in s2, a nonlinearity and the data feeds; award_voting (KEEP_PRIMARY) and award_vote_rank_model are overlapping descriptions of one model; season_sim is audited 'a source of team success probabilities rather than an input to votes' but is the only game_context_script coverage.

Interaction 'award_vote_rank_model x m.rules_text x award_timing' multiplies two independent events (rank top-3, finalists announced), which is a product, not an interaction; the real test is whether announcement timing depends on the field. Triple Crown correlations (HR-RBI about 0.6, AVG-HR 0.1-0.2) and the '1.5 sd' collapse are stated without a cited basis.

transactions.rederivation_notes: My own chain, with no live series here (KXMLBNEXTTEAM is in participation; KXMLBCOACH is title-only in off-field). From the NEXTTEAM text: one market per team plus Retires/No Team; stays with current team resolves Yes for it; free agent signing with any team including the former counts; extension with the same team does not resolve early; resolution at Mar 25 2027. Mechanism: eligibility (contract end, options, opt-outs, QO), whether a move occurs (hazard by calendar, team incentives), WHO/WHERE (categorical destination choice: positional need, payroll space, competing bidders, player preference, re-sign probability), report-to-official lag, plus the labour calendar (CBA expires Dec 1 2026; lockout widely expected; transaction freeze). Manager hires: vacancy hazard plus candidate selection. Required inputs: contract status, calendar, team payroll/need, destination model, report credibility, labour status. After reading: contract_status, calendar hazard and report reliability are sensible. Missed: destination/candidate selection, lockout regime, and an unsupported 'official announcement' settlement assumption.

findings.text: No destination/selection stage. KXMLBNEXTTEAM resolves one market per team and KXMLBCOACH per candidate, so the object is a categorical choice (which of 30 teams, or retire, or which person is hired), not just whether/when a transaction occurs. The record models only eligibility, timing hazards and payroll headroom, and dismisses opponent_matchup and environment as N/A ('rival team's competition ... handled through payroll headroom'). Missing inputs: positional need, competing bidders, market size/ownership spending, player preference/hometown, qualifying-offer and re-sign probability; for managers, the candidate pool, interview reports and GM/coach connections.

Labour-stoppage regime missing. The CBA expires at 11:59 pm ET on Dec 1 2026 and a lockout the next day is widely expected (web check: 2021-22 lockout ran to Mar 10 2022 and froze 40-man-roster transactions). A 'next team before Mar 25 2027' market is therefore a mixture of a pre-expiry rush, a frozen window of unknown length and a post-deal rush; calendar_hazard_by_event_type fits 15 years that include one such stoppage. Add a labour_status input (negotiation state, lockout flag and expected end, rules during lockout) and the unresolved item.

Settlement assumed, not read. variants_and_edge_cases and s5 state contracts 'typically require the official transaction', that 'a reported agreement subject to a physical does not resolve until official; medical failure can void'. The only NEXTTEAM text seen (quote in the participation record) says 'signs a contract with any team' and is truncated; nothing sampled mentions announcement, physicals or voiding. The core of s4/s5 (report credibility vs official event) depends on this and is not listed as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS; rules_evidence is empty.

Archetype is a shell. Zero live series; the trade, call-up, extension, non-tender and Rule 5 markets in the target text have no ledger series at all, so most of the calendar-anchor design is for contracts nobody trades here. The two real contracts sit in participation and off-field, producing three overlapping records with different input sets.

Benchmark/weak items kept. m.quote_history is BENCHMARK_ONLY but is a stage input (s5) and in required_data feeds; offfield_base_rate is WEAK yet used in distribution_variance coverage and a feed; season_sim is KEEP_SECONDARY with reason 'duplicates seller_buyer_status in use' (should be a duplicate verdict). Thresholds such as 'playoff odds about 10-20%' are invented.

unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials.rederivation_notes: My own chain from the 15 sampled rules. Player ladders: KXMLBOUTS (starter with at least one pitch), KXMLBERA/KXMLBWA (starter with at least one batter faced), KXMLBSB (starter with at least one plate appearance); non-qualifying cases pay fair market price. Team order statistics: best/worst record by win%, longest losing streak, most team strikeouts, with $1/N rounded-down tie splits and no tiebreakers. Individual-season: 50 HR and 40 SB regular season only; 107+ mph pitch in any game including playoffs. Schedule events: first game of 2027 before May 31, games played above 600, exact series score. Mechanisms: opportunity times conversion; league extremes via a joint simulation of 30 teams; extreme-value for speed; series sequences; and for 2027 markets, the labour calendar (CBA expires Dec 1 2026, lockout expected). Required inputs: shared pitcher/hitter inputs, team talent posterior and schedule, ROS projections, high-end velocity data, series model, labour status. After reading: the engine decomposition is sensible. Missed: the lockout hazard behind OPENINGDAY/SEASONGAMES, mapping duplicates, methods labelled as inputs.

findings.text: Labour-stoppage misdiagnosed as a typo. KXMLBOPENINGDAY ('first game in the 2027 ... season ... prior to May 31, 2027') and KXMLBSEASONGAMES ('above 600 games in the 2027 MLB regular season') are tails of a CBA lockout: the agreement expires Dec 1 2026, a lockout is widely expected, and in 2021-22 a lockout postponed opening day a week (web check). A 600-game strike (about a quarter of 2,430) is a plausible 'season substantially lost' threshold, not an obvious error. The record calls it 'trivially true ... a wording or strike error' and s5 says opening day is 'set by league announcement ... near-deterministic' with inputs only m.rules_text. Required: a labour_status input (negotiation state, lockout start/end hazard, games lost under shortened-season scenarios) and rewriting unr_games_strike.

Duplication and mapping. KXMLBOUTS, KXMLBERA and KXMLBWA are the only live series for pitcher_outs and pitcher_earned_runs_hits_walks (both NO_LIVE_SERIES), and KXMLBSB belongs with hitter_rbis_runs_sb. s2 re-derives them in two sentences and defers to 'sibling records', so rules are verified here while the inputs live in siblings that cannot cite the rules. The record also contradicts its sibling on a settlement case: here 'an injury on the first pitch settles outs at zero but refunds walks', while ERHW says an immediate injury 'still settles on tiny counts'; the text defines neither (a starter with a pitch but no batter faced). Flag CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS and fix the series mapping.

Methods labelled as inputs. team_season_extreme_engine, series_exact_score_distribution and joint_season_hr_sb_distribution are simulation engines (the season_futures record calls mlb.season_sim 'a method ... not an input'), while the actual required inputs for the extremes (a 30-team talent posterior with vintages, remaining schedule, projection vintages) are not defined here and are only reported as unresolved (unr_no_inputs_for_extremes); they are defined in season_futures. mlb.pa_sim and the WEAK mlb.leash remain in s2/stage inputs.

Fastest-pitch model extrapolates beyond observed data. 'Exponential tail ... P(max >= 107) = 1 - exp(-N p)' fits a top-1% tail to a threshold that, to my knowledge, no tracked pitch has reached (record roughly 105-106 mph; unverified), so the physical ceiling matters more than an exponential tail; reliever max-effort pitch counts and playoff exposure are noted but tracking-source/calibration differences between Statcast release speed and broadcast speed are only an unresolved SOURCE_UNVERIFIED. Category label 'pace_volume' for this input is wrong. P(any) = 1 - prod(1 - p_i) assumes independence across pitchers.

Generic stat series unseen: KXMLBTEAMSTAT ('Team Stat'), KXMLBSTAT ('Season Stat') and KXMLBSTATCOUNT are generic families; only most-strikeouts, 107 mph and 50 HR/40 SB were sampled, and the engine is built around team strikeouts. Other stat variants are not flagged CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS. KXMLBLSTREAK's streak model assumes independent game sequences without discussing postponed or suspended games.
